   - `publication_year`: 4-digit year printed on the paper/report itself (e.g. `"2024"`), or `"not reported"` if undated. Give exact page/header in `where_found`.
   - `country`: Country or countries studied as stated in the paper (use semicolon-separated names if multiple specific countries, or exact global/regional scope as stated, e.g. `"Global (48 countries)"`), or `"not reported"`.
   - `sample_size`: Exact sample size(s) AND explicit unit(s) of analysis stated in the paper (e.g. `"593 households across 4 neighbourhoods"`, `"128 municipalities; 2,048 observations (2010-2025)"`, `"32 semi-structured interviews"`), or `"not reported"` if pure doctrinal/legal analysis with no empirical sample.
   - `study_design`: Study design as the authors describe it and as operationalized in the methods section (be specific about quantitative/qualitative/quasi-experimental/experimental/review structure).
   - `effect_estimate`: Headline result of the study regarding how the legal, administrative, regulatory, institutional, tenure, tariff/subsidy, or participation factor relates to water/sanitation access/outcomes, with exact printed numbers (point estimates, units, 95% CIs, p-values, sample N) if quantitative, or concise factual headline finding if qualitative (noting `"Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported"` when purely qualitative), in your own words from the paper alone.
   - `risk_of_bias_tool`: Pick the single design-matched tool per `RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1:
     * `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"` (individually randomized trial)
     * `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"` (cluster-randomized trial — check unit of randomization carefully!)
     * `"ROBINS-I"` (non-randomized intervention / quasi-experimental study with a genuine comparator: DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, policy panel FE)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"` (quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without quasi-experimental intervention comparator)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"` (observational longitudinal cohort study without intervention framing)
     * `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"` (primary qualitative study: interviews, focus groups, ethnography, qualitative case study)
     * `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"` (genuine mixed-methods study combining both qualitative and quantitative primary components)
     * `"AMSTAR 2"` (systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with systematic search/screening; NEVER use for non-systematic narrative literature reviews)
     * `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"` (legal-empirical, doctrinal-empirical, jurimetric, or institutional-historical study that fits none of the six conventional designs above)
     * `"NONE"` (fits none of the listed tools, e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model, or non-systematic narrative review/essay without primary empirical data or systematic search — explain why in `comment`)
   - `mechanism_certainty`: Single integer `"0"`, `"1"`, `"2"`, `"3"`, or `"4"` strictly obeying `CODEBOOK.md` §9 and its design ceiling:
     * `"4"` ONLY for randomized trials (`RoB 2`)
     * `"3"` ONLY for `RoB 2` trials OR `ROBINS-I` studies with credible Low/Moderate overall risk of bias
     * All other designs (cross-sectional/JBI, cohort, qualitative/CASP, mixed-methods/MMAT, systematic review/AMSTAR 2, Legal Framework, NONE, or Serious/Critical ROBINS-I) CANNOT exceed `"2"`! (`"2"` = mechanism directly observed empirically; `"1"` = documented statistical/descriptive association; `"0"` = inferred only by authors).

country.comment: Empirical fieldwork and spatial household survey conducted in the coastal town of Mbour, Senegal (national Water Access Index reference values for Mauritania and Mali from ChartsBin 2011 are briefly cited for background comparison only on PDF p. 6).
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title, Abstract, and Section 1

effect_estimate.comment: Descriptive spatial proportions and tariff comparisons only; no multivariable regression estimates, 95% confidence intervals, or p-values are reported in the paper. Water poverty prevalence (52.4% of water-paying families; 26.6% unaffected) is cited in Section 3.3 from Toure (2009), the lead author's master's dissertation on which this paper is based.
effect_estimate.value: 48.7% of the surveyed population is connected to the SDE piped water distribution network (~50% has no access to a water supply system) and 38.6% uses well water; income poverty (<600 Francs CFA/day) affects 62% of the population, water poverty (water cost >5% of monthly income) affects 52.4% of water-paying families, and the majority of the population experiences very low water availability (Water Access Index 0–0.25 m3/person/day). Uncontrolled urban expansion and SDE service-boundary limits leave peripheral neighborhoods unserved, while unconnected households face standpipe water tariffs of 1,750 Francs CFA/m3 compared with the SDE social tariff rate of 191 Francs CFA/m3.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 4–6, Sections 3.1–3.4 and Figs. 6–11; PDF p. 7, Section 4

mechanism_certainty.comment: Cross-sectional spatial survey (ceiling = 2). Assigned 1 because the study documents descriptive spatial associations between SDE service-area coverage, unplanned urban expansion, income/water poverty, tariff differentials (1,750 vs. 191 Francs CFA/m3), and household water access, while asserting the perverse effect of the 1995 Senegalese water sector reform without directly observing utility administrative/legal decision-making processes.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 3, Section 2; PDF p. 4, Section 3.1; PDF p. 7, Section 4

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines limits of the SDE utility distribution network in reaching city boundaries/rural Malicounda encroachment (service_area), uncontrolled urban growth where habitation preceded urbanization in unparceled/squatter areas (planning), and prohibitive standpipe water pricing of 1,750 vs. 191 Francs CFA/m3 SDE social tariff alongside >5% monthly income expenditure burden (fees). Governance integration issues and the 1995 water sector reform are noted in the Abstract/Introduction as framing context rather than empirically analyzed.
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF p. 3, Section 2; PDF p. 4, Section 3.1; PDF pp. 6–7, Section 3.3 and Section 4

outcome_flags.comment: Measures household connection to the SDE distribution network (formal_connection), overall access to water systems vs. wells/standpipes (water_access), spatial extent of SDE network coverage across Mbour (service_coverage), daily per-capita water withdrawal volume via the Water Access Index in m3/person/day (service_quantity), and water expenditure share >5% of monthly income plus tariff burden (affordability). Water quality and sanitation are mentioned contextually without separate empirical outcome metrics reported in Results.

publication_year.comment: Journal header states Vol. 14 (2012) pp. 33–39 (article history notes Received 15 September 2010, Accepted 10 August 2011, and © 2011 Elsevier B.V.).
publication_year.where_found: PDF p. 1, journal header ('14 (2012) 33–39'); running headers on PDF pp. 2–7

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Primary empirical design is a quantitative cross-sectional spatial household survey (N = 120 households across a 500 m grid) mapping associations between poverty and water access indicators without a quasi-experimental comparator. Although Section 2.1 notes interviews with officials from four institutions, no qualitative interview methods, sample size, or qualitative findings are reported, so JBI Analytical Cross Sectional rather than MMAT applies.
risk_of_bias_tool.value: JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies

sample_size.comment: One household was surveyed at the centroid of each 500 m spatial grid cell (excluding 1 cell covering the municipal soccer stadium), totaling 120 households with a 99.19% response rate (estimated >1,000 persons based on Senegal's mean household size of 9.8). Interviews were also conducted with officials from Senegal National Water Company, Mbour Hall, Senegal Prevision and Statistics Department, and Direction of Water Resources Management and Planning (exact count of interviewees not reported).
sample_size.value: 120 households (99.19% response rate; estimated >1,000 persons across 500 m spatial grid cells in Mbour), plus interviews with officials from 4 institutions (number of interviewees not reported)

study_design.comment: Two-stage spatial observational study combining Kompsat satellite imagery and a systematic/probabilistic 500 m mesh household survey (analyzed in SPSS and mapped via ArcGIS thematic interpolation) with background institutional interviews and review of bimonthly water invoices/container volumes.
study_design.value: Cross-sectional spatial household survey (systematic 500 m grid sampling without replacement) with satellite imagery, GIS thematic spatial analysis, descriptive statistics, and supplementary institutional official interviews
study_design.where_found: PDF pp. 2–3, Section 1, Section 2, and Section 2.1
